/opt/homebrew/bin/tshark -r "$PCAP" -q -z io,phs 2>/dev/null | head -30

# Victim host identity - DHCP hostname
echo "=== DHCP hostnames and MAC addresses ==="
/opt/homebrew/bin/tshark -r "$PCAP" -Y "dhcp" -T fields -e dhcp.option.hostname -e dhcp.hw.mac_addr -e ip.src 2>/dev/null | sort -u

PCAP="/Users/yaakulyasabbani/Documents/GitHub/latex_researchpapers/Skill_Issue_LLM_PCAP_Forensics/datasets/evidence/mta-2025-01-22/2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap"

# Get Windows username from Kerberos
echo "=== Kerberos client names (Windows users) ==="
/opt/homebrew/bin/tshark -r "$PCAP" -Y "kerberos.CNameString" -T fields -e kerberos.CNameString 2>/dev/null | sort -u

PCAP="/Users/yaakulyasabbani/Documents/GitHub/latex_researchpapers/Skill_Issue_LLM_PCAP_Forensics/datasets/evidence/mta-2025-01-22/2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap"

# IP conversations - top by bytes
echo "=== Top IP conversations by bytes ==="
/opt/homebrew/bin/tshark -r "$PCAP" -q -z conv,ip 2>/dev/null | head -50

PCAP="/Users/yaakulyasabbani/Documents/GitHub/latex_researchpapers/Skill_Issue_LLM_PCAP_Forensics/datasets/evidence/mta-2025-01-22/2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap"

# DNS queries to see what domains are being resolved
echo "=== DNS queries from 10.1.17.215 ==="
/opt/homebrew/bin/tshark -r "$PCAP" -Y "dns.qry.name and ip.src==10.1.17.215" -T fields -e dns.qry.name 2>/dev/null | sort -u | head -50

PCAP="/Users/yaakulyasabbani/Documents/GitHub/latex_researchpapers/Skill_Issue_LLM_PCAP_Forensics/datasets/evidence/mta-2025-01-22/2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap"

# HTTP requests from the suspicious IPs
echo "=== HTTP requests from 10.1.17.215 ==="
/opt/homebrew/bin/tshark -r "$PCAP" -Y "http.request and ip.src==10.1.17.215" -T fields -e ip.dst -e http.host -e http.request.method -e http.request.uri 2>/dev/null | head -50

PCAP="/Users/yaakulyasabbani/Documents/GitHub/latex_researchpapers/Skill_Issue_LLM_PCAP_Forensics/datasets/evidence/mta-2025-01-22/2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap"

# See if 10.1.17.2 and 10.1.17.215 are the same machine - check NetBIOS
echo "=== ARP to find which IP is the victim machine ==="
/opt/homebrew/bin/tshark -r "$PCAP" -Y "arp" -T fields -e arp.src.proto_ipv4 -e arp.src.hw_mac -e arp.dst.proto_ipv4 -e arp.dst.hw_mac 2>/dev/null | sort -u

PCAP="/Users/yaakulyasabbani/Documents/GitHub/latex_researchpapers/Skill_Issue_LLM_PCAP_Forensics/datasets/evidence/mta-2025-01-22/2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap"

# Look at POST requests which might be C2 communication
echo "=== POST requests from 10.1.17.215 ==="
/opt/homebrew/bin/tshark -r "$PCAP" -Y "http.request.method==POST and ip.src==10.1.17.215" -T fields -e frame.number -e ip.dst -e http.host -e http.request.uri 2>/dev/null | head -30

PCAP="/Users/yaakulyasabbani/Documents/GitHub/latex_researchpapers/Skill_Issue_LLM_PCAP_Forensics/datasets/evidence/mta-2025-01-22/2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap"

# Look at TLS/HTTPS connections - check SNI
echo "=== TLS Server Name Indication (HTTPS) from 10.1.17.215 ==="
/opt/homebrew/bin/tshark -r "$PCAP" -Y "tls.handshake.type==1 and ip.src==10.1.17.215" -T fields -e frame.number -e ip.dst -e tls.handshake.extensions_server_name 2>/dev/null | head -50

PCAP="/Users/yaakulyasabbani/Documents/GitHub/latex_researchpapers/Skill_Issue_LLM_PCAP_Forensics/datasets/evidence/mta-2025-01-22/2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap"

# Get more details on the C2 connection to 5.252.153.241 - examine TCP stream
echo "=== TCP streams to 5.252.153.241 ==="
/opt/homebrew/bin/tshark -r "$PCAP" -Y "ip.dst==5.252.153.241" -T fields -e frame.number -e tcp.srcport -e tcp.dstport -e tcp.flags.syn -e tcp.flags.ack 2>/dev/null | head -30

PCAP="/Users/yaakulyasabbani/Documents/GitHub/latex_researchpapers/Skill_Issue_LLM_PCAP_Forensics/datasets/evidence/mta-2025-01-22/2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap"

# Export HTTP objects to examine potential malware downloads
mkdir -p /tmp/pcap_objects
/opt/homebrew/bin/tshark -r "$PCAP" --export-objects "http,/tmp/pcap_objects" -q 2>/dev/null

echo "=== Exported objects ==="
ls -lah /tmp/pcap_objects/ | head -30

PCAP="/Users/yaakulyasabbani/Documents/GitHub/latex_researchpapers/Skill_Issue_LLM_PCAP_Forensics/datasets/evidence/mta-2025-01-22/2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap"

# Look at the beaconing pattern - repeated requests to the C2
echo "=== HTTP GET requests to 5.252.153.241 with URI details ==="
/opt/homebrew/bin/tshark -r "$PCAP" -Y "http.request and ip.src==10.1.17.215 and ip.dst==5.252.153.241" -T fields -e frame.time -e http.request.method -e http.request.uri 2>/dev/null | sort -u | head -30

PCAP="/Users/yaakulyasabbani/Documents/GitHub/latex_researchpapers/Skill_Issue_LLM_PCAP_Forensics/datasets/evidence/mta-2025-01-22/2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap"

# Check for the suspicious domains we saw in TLS
echo "=== Suspicious HTTPS connections ==="
/opt/homebrew/bin/tshark -r "$PCAP" -Y "tls.handshake.type==1 and ip.src==10.1.17.215" -T fields -e ip.dst -e tls.handshake.extensions_server_name 2>/dev/null | grep -E "authenticatoor|appointedtime|google-authenticator|burleson"

PCAP="/Users/yaakulyasabbani/Documents/GitHub/latex_researchpapers/Skill_Issue_LLM_PCAP_Forensics/datasets/evidence/mta-2025-01-22/2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap"

# Check traffic to 45.125.66.32
echo "=== HTTP requests to 45.125.66.32 ==="
/opt/homebrew/bin/tshark -r "$PCAP" -Y "http.request and ip.src==10.1.17.215 and ip.dst==45.125.66.32" -T fields -e frame.time -e http.request.method -e http.request.uri 2>/dev/null | head -30

PCAP="/Users/yaakulyasabbani/Documents/GitHub/latex_researchpapers/Skill_Issue_LLM_PCAP_Forensics/datasets/evidence/mta-2025-01-22/2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap"
